title: Rights and the rule of law

stops.title: No one is above the law

listen.explanationKey: What does the Bill of Rights protect?
facts: The Constitution was written in 1787. Many Americans wanted it to say clearly which rights the government can never take away.
So in 1791, ten amendments were added to the Constitution. These first ten amendments are called the Bill of Rights.
It protects the basic rights of Americans and of people living in the United States.
Freedom of speech and freedom of religion are two of these rights.

newWords.meaning: the first ten amendments to the Constitution
the right to say what you think

readIt.sentence: What is one right in the Bill of Rights?

writeIt.sentence: Freedom of speech is one right.

lessons.title: No one is above the law

listen.explanationKey: What is the rule of law?
facts: The rule of law means everyone must follow the law. Leaders and the government must obey the law too.
No one is above the law. For example, the President must pay taxes like everyone else. A mayor who steals can be arrested and go to court like anyone else.
The government has three branches so one part does not become too powerful. Each branch can check the others. This is called checks and balances.
For example, Congress writes laws, the President can veto them, and the courts can decide a law goes against the Constitution.

newWords.meaning: each branch can limit the power of the others
the power of government is split into parts

writeIt.sentence: We elect the President and Congress.

listen.explanationKey: What is the form of government of the United States?
facts: The United States is a republic: the people vote for leaders, and those leaders make laws for them.
This is also called a representative democracy. “Representative” means the leaders speak and act for the people who elected them.
It is also a constitution-based federal republic: the Constitution is the highest law, and power is shared between the national government and the states.
The economic system of the United States is capitalism, also called a free market economy. People and businesses can own things and decide what to make, buy and sell.
Think of a supermarket: stores choose what to sell and what price to ask, and you choose what to buy. Most of the time, the government does not decide this for you. That is a free market.

newWords.meaning: a country where the people elect their leaders
an economy where people and businesses own and run things
when people and businesses, not the government, decide what to make, sell and buy

readIt.sentence: Who can vote in the United States?

writeIt.sentence: Citizens have the right to vote.
